dialect: Modern Standard Arabic (fuṣḥā), the widely taught standard; Arabic script, terms fully vowelled, other target text partly vowelled

profile.noun_citation: bare singular, with vowel marks on terms
profile.grammar_notes: No present-tense copula: identity and description are verbless nominal sentences (أَنَا طَالِبٌ); كَانَ supplies past/future 'be'. Negation of present nominal sentences with لَيْسَ (conjugated), of present verbs with لَا, past with لَمْ + jussive or مَا + past, future with لَنْ. Existence with هُنَاكَ / يُوجَدُ. Possession has no verb: عِنْدَ + attached pronoun (عِنْدِي 'I have'), also لِ / مَعَ. Location with فِي and other prepositions. Questions: هَلْ for yes/no; question words مَا/مَاذَا, مَنْ, أَيْنَ, مَتَى, كَيْفَ, لِمَاذَا, كَمْ. Modality via verbs + أَنْ: يُرِيدُ أَنْ (want), يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ (can), يَجِبُ أَنْ (must). Motion: ذَهَبَ/يَذْهَبُ (go), جَاءَ/يَجِيءُ (come). Verbs are cited in the past 3rd masc. sing. (dictionary form) or taught with the present stem. Future with سَـ / سَوْفَ. Politeness is not grammatical; formulae (مِنْ فَضْلِكَ, شُكْرًا). Closed sets: independent pronouns (12 incl. dual), attached pronoun suffixes, question words, demonstratives (هٰذَا/هٰذِهِ/ذٰلِكَ/تِلْكَ…), the definite article ال (attached), gender and dual marking.
